h1: How time outside the UK affects your ILR and citizenship application
intro: Time outside the UK is one of the most common reasons settlement and citizenship applications run into trouble. Here’s how the limits work, the mistakes people make, and how to check your own trips.

sections.heading: The limits for time outside the UK
sections.text:
- Indefinite Leave to Remain: no more than 180 days in any rolling 12-month period, for most routes
- British citizenship: no more than 450 days in the 5 years before you apply, and 90 days in the last 12 months
- Citizenship if married to a British citizen: 270 days in 3 years, and 90 days in the last 12 months

sections.heading: Rolling 12 months, not calendar years
sections.text: The ILR limit applies to any 12-month period, not each calendar year. Two long trips either side of New Year can break the limit even if neither calendar year does.

sections.heading: Which days count as time outside the UK?
sections.text: The days you leave and return don’t count. Only whole days spent abroad are counted.

sections.heading: Check your trips in minutes
sections.text: Our free [absence calculator](/absence-calculator/) checks your time outside the UK against each limit. If you’re over, there may still be options: [book a consultation](/contact-us/).

sections.heading: Keeping a record of your trips
sections.text: Keep a simple list of every trip: the date you left and the date you came back. Passport stamps, boarding passes and booking emails all help. The Home Office may check your travel history, so your list needs to be accurate.

sections.heading: Planning around the limits
sections.text: If you’re close to a limit, plan future trips carefully until you’ve applied. Applying a little later, once an old trip falls outside the period, can sometimes solve the problem.

faqs.q: Does a weekend trip count as time outside the UK?
faqs.a: Only the whole days abroad count, not the days you leave and return.

faqs.q: Can the Home Office ignore some absences?
faqs.a: In some cases, such as serious illness or compassionate reasons, with evidence.

faqs.q: Does time outside the UK affect citizenship differently?
faqs.a: Yes. Citizenship has its own limits over 5 years (or 3), plus 90 days in the last 12 months.

title: Time Outside the UK: ILR and Citizenship Limits
description: How time outside the UK affects ILR and British citizenship: the 180-day, 450-day and 90-day limits, rolling 12 months, and how to check your trips.
